title: feat(spec,objectql,runtime): declare HookContext.referentialCascadeDelete, the delete twin of referentialFieldClear
body:
Fixes #23221

Clause-②: yes

## What

Declares `HookContext.referentialCascadeDelete`, the delete twin of `referentialFieldClear`. The engine sets it on every child delete its cascade issues, and it is carried into the QuickJS sandbox by contract.

- `true` exactly on each child delete that `cascadeDeleteRelations` issues for a relation whose `deleteBehavior` resolves to `cascade`, in both phases (`beforeDelete`, `afterDelete`) and at any depth: a grandchild that the child's own cascade removes is marked too.
- Absent, never `false`, on every other dispatch. That covers the delete the caller asked for, a hand delete of the same child, the `set_null` cleanup update (which keeps `referentialFieldClear` and never carries this key), and any write a cascaded child's hooks issue through `ctx.api`, deletes included.
- Named consumers: HotCRM's freeze guards on quote lines and deal lines (objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2078, ruling C). With the key, a guard can refuse a hand delete of a settled line and yield to the parent's cascade.

## Where it landed, and one departure from the dispatch's mechanism assumption

The landing sites are the card's: `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts` beside `referentialFieldClear`; `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (the cascade child-delete site, the `delete()` hook-context assembly, and a helper beside `buildReferentialFieldClear`); `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/` (`body-runner.ts` `buildSandboxContext`, `quickjs-runner.ts` `installCtx`, `script-runner.ts` `ScriptContext`).

The dispatch assumed the engine would stamp a `__` marker on the child delete's context, which is the twin's trust model. I measured that route and did not take it, for two reasons:

1. **It would leak into the child's hook writes.** `buildHookApi(opCtx.context)` hands the delete's own context object to `ScopedContext`, whose repositories pass it unchanged into every write (`ObjectRepository.deleteById` / `delete` / `update`), and `ObjectQL.transaction` spreads it (`{ ...baseContext, transaction }`). So a key stamped on the child's context rides into every write the child's hooks issue through `ctx.api`. A hook's own delete during the cascade would then read as cascade-issued, which contradicts "true exactly on each child delete the cascade issues, absent on every other dispatch".
2. **It would change what the child is handed.** A stamp needs a fresh object, `{ ...(context ?? {}), __x: true }`. Where no transaction is opened, that turns an absent caller context into a present one, and both `buildSession(undefined)` (returns `undefined`) and `buildHookApi(undefined)` (falls back to `{ isSystem: true }`) would move. The engine already rejected a context key for the sibling cascade state for exactly this reason; see the `cascadeDeleteSets` docblock.

**What I did instead.** The walk issues each child delete inside an engine-private `AsyncLocalStorage` token that names that child's object and id (`cascadeIssuedDeletes`, beside `cascadeDeleteSets`). `delete()` claims a matching, unclaimed token once, before any middleware or hook runs, and projects it onto the declared key. The context still reaches the child by reference and unchanged, as before.

**Consequence for the contract** (written into the docblock and the changeset): this fact has no operation-private spelling at all. The declared key is the only channel, and there is nothing on `ctx.api`, `ctx.transaction` or a `__` key to sniff instead, so the objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1165 ruling holds by construction. The key is a signal to app code, not an authorization input: each child delete is still authorized as the caller, and plugin-security reads nothing new.

## Pins, one per face

- **spec** `packages/spec/src/data/hook.test.ts`: the key survives a parse, typed; it is absent (not `false`) when not carried; and it is a key of its own (neither twin appears on the other's parsed context).
- **objectql** `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete.test.ts`, new `describe` with 6 cases:
  - the cascaded child carries the key in both phases, beside the inherited caller identity; the hand delete of the same child under the same identity, and the root delete, carry no key;
  - a grandchild removed by the child's cascade is marked;
  - in the same cascade, the `set_null` cleanup carries `referentialFieldClear` and not this key, and the cascaded child carries this key and not `referentialFieldClear`;
  - a delete and an update that a cascaded child's hooks issue through `ctx.api` are not marked;
  - a delete of the very same row from inside the cascaded dispatch finds the token already claimed;
  - an identity-less cascade still marks its child and puts no `__` key on the envelope.
- **runtime** `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/referential-cascade-delete-signal.integration.test.ts`: real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3) + `QuickJSScriptRunner` behind `hookBodyRunnerFactory`. A shipped body reads `ctx.referentialCascadeDelete === true` on the cascaded line in both phases, with the inherited `session.userId` present; on the hand delete of a sibling line under the same identity it reads the key as absent (`typeof` is `'undefined'`).
- **cli** `packages/cli/test/lowered-body-face-enumeration.test.ts` derives both the in-process face and the body face from source, so it is a reader of this change. It stays green because the key is present on both faces.

## Ablations (one-shot, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` WRAP mode)

Each mutation was proven on disk (anchor 1 to 0, blob changed) and each restore was proven equal to the HEAD blob with an empty `git diff HEAD`. All five targets are reached through relative source imports, so no rebuild was needed. Expected directions were written down before running.

| # | Mutation | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | delete the `delete()` projection spread (`engine.ts`) | the 6 new objectql pins red | 6 failed / 19 passed |
| A2 | delete the `buildSandboxContext` carrier (`body-runner.ts`) | runtime pin red | 1 failed |
| A3 | delete the `installCtx` `setProp` (`quickjs-runner.ts`) | runtime pin red | 1 failed |
| A4 | delete `issued.claimed = true` (`engine.ts`) | only the same-row pin red | 1 failed / 24 passed |
| A5 | delete the object/id key check (`engine.ts`) | green: no reachable mismatch | 25 passed |

A5 is a characterisation, not a pin. The check is a stated defensive invariant, and it has no reachable counter-case at this head: the claim runs before any middleware or hook, so nothing can enter `delete()` inside the token scope first. See Acceptance notes.

## Gates

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, which takes the change set from the merge base: 11 paths, +671/-1, 115 commands. Every command was run byte for byte from that list, its exit recorded before any pipe, and the record reconciled with `--ran`.

- **Final head `7e4509b6cb`:** 115 derived, 115 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN; `--ran` exit 0. All 115 commands exit 0.
- **At `670114eec`, the same list:** 4 refusals, each fixed and none of them a finding.
  - `check-engine-split-ratio.mjs --days 90` (exit 2) and `check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` (exit 3) refused on the shallow clone. After `git fetch --shallow-since=2026-07-09 origin main`, both exit 0.

- **Families CI runs** are cited from the PR's check-runs in the report, not re-run here.

Those commits change 6 gate-script files and `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, one line away from this branch's one-line addition there, so the merge is textual-clean. CI's `check:authorable-surface` runs on the merge ref.

## Acceptance notes

- **The object/id key check in `claimReferentialCascadeDelete`** is kept as a defensive invariant ("the delete that claims the token is the one the walk issued"). Ablation A5 shows nothing at this head can reach a mismatch. Claim-once (A4) is the pinned half.
- **Liveness ledger: no row is needed.** `HookContextSchema` is the runtime hook context, not a registered metadata type. `packages/spec/liveness/hook.json` covers `HookSchema`'s 15 authored keys only, and the update twin has no row either. `check:liveness` is green.
- **Generated faces:** `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json` gains `data/HookContext:referentialCascadeDelete` (from the spec build), and `content/docs/references/data/hook.mdx` gains its row (`check:generated --fix`, where `check:docs` was the only artifact proved stale). `authorable-surface.base.json` is untouched.
- **`engine.ts` regions touched:** the `CascadeIssuedDelete` interface (about :4131), the `cascadeIssuedDeletes` field (about :4292), `claimReferentialCascadeDelete` (about :6407), the cascade site (about :18750) and the `delete()` claim and projection (about :18880 and :18915). The serial constraint named PR #23412's regions (:5514, :8856, :20839); that PR has since landed on `main`, and this branch merged it cleanly.
- **No behaviour moves for anything but the new key.** The child delete is still handed the caller's context by reference, and no authorization path reads the token.
- **No ADR governs** the hook-context referential markers or the cascade dispatch's hook semantics (checked: `docs/adr` names neither `referentialFieldClear` nor `cascadeDeleteRelations`).
